fixes.explanation: Idols, friend. God says, "You also took the fine jewelry of gold and silver I had given you, and you made male idols with which to prostitute yourself." The gold and silver came from God's hands, and she used it to make idols. That's a heavy verse.

That's not what the text says, friend. God says she turned to the Assyrians, "…because you were not yet satisfied. Even after that, you were still not satisfied." So after the Assyrians, she was still not satisfied.

Pay, friend. God says, "I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers." Back in verse 34, He says, "you paid a fee instead of receiving one." That paying is what God says will never happen again.
Canaanites, friend. God says, "Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites." That's where God starts Jerusalem's story.

Not even one, friend. God says, "No one cared enough for you to do even one of these things out of compassion for you." The cord, the washing, the salt and the cloths all got skipped. That's a heavy part, and the text says none of them.

It's true, friend, and I wish it weren't. God says, "…you were thrown out into the open field, because you were despised on the day of your birth." The verse also says no one cared enough to do those acts of compassion for her. That's a heavy part, so let's sit with it a second.
The text never says that, friend. God sees her lying in her blood and says to her, "Live!" Nothing there sends her anywhere. Then He says, "I made you thrive like a plant of the field."
That's not what the text says, friend. God pledges Himself to her and enters into a covenant with her. Then He says, "…you became Mine…"

A crown, friend. God says, "I put a ring in your nose, earrings on your ears, and a beautiful crown upon your head." He keeps adding to the outfit. Meanwhile all I've got on my head is a tall white hat, and I'm proud of that hat.
The text points somewhere else, friend. God says her beauty "…was perfect in the splendor I bestowed on you…" Bestowed means God gave it to her.
True. God says, "…because of your fame, you trusted in your beauty…" Her trust landed on her beauty. That's the turn in the story, friend.
No neighbor names in that verse, friend. God says she did not remember "…the days of your youth when you were naked and bare, wallowing in your own blood." That's what God says she did not remember.
The opposite, friend. God says she made a lofty shrine "…in every public square." Then He says, "At the head of every street you built your lofty shrines…" That's where the text puts them.
Right, friend. God says, "…you were not yet satisfied. Even after that, you were still not satisfied." That's the Assyrians, after Egypt. She keeps reaching and keeps coming up empty.
She does the opposite, friend. God says she bribed her lovers "…to come to you from everywhere…" She was drawing them in, and she paid them to come. Nothing in the verse has her sending them away.
True. God says, "…I will sentence you to the punishment of women who commit adultery and those who shed blood…" Both are named. This is a heavy verse.
Down they go, friend. God says her lovers "…will level your mounds and tear down your lofty shrines." The mounds are leveled and the lofty shrines are torn down. What she built up is what comes down.
No guards here, friend. God says her lovers will level her mounds and tear down her lofty shrines. That's tearing down, not guarding.
Not find, friend. God says, "I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will never again pay your lovers." The word is pay. Back in verse 34, He says, "you paid a fee instead of receiving one."
